newsitem.title: UK: Tanzania 97/98 coffee crop seen hit by weather.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania 97/98 coffee crop seen hit by weather.

text.p: Tanzania's sales of new crop coffee may be completed by April given 1996/97's fairly small crop while unfavourable weather has raised concerns about the 1997/98 prospects, Swiss coffee firm Schluter Trading said.

It said in its latest African coffee crop report that the first main Kenyan crop offerings had been of generally good quality while in Uganda rains in the past month had hampered the drying of new crop in the central area.
In Tanzania, Schulter said the first eight auctions of new crop had seen the sale in total of 226,000 60-kg bags.
"Given this year's fairly small crop, the auctions are likely to be finished by April, leaving a gap till probably August for next crop's coffee," it said.
A company official put Tanzania's total 1996/97 crop at 650,000 bags compared with an average of around 833,000 bags in the 1970s and 1980s.
"So far the rains have been rather patchy in the south, and in the north have been poor, so there is some concern about the prospects for the 1997/98 crop," the report said.
Schluter said the main Kenyan crop should start to appear in volume from around mid-January.
It said the first main crop offerings had been of generally good quality, though it was still very early in the season.
The company said the rains in Uganda in the past month had been good, but that in turn has slowed the drying of the new crop coffee in the central area.
"However, these are now beginning to appear in larger volume in Kampala, and this will be moving out in the coming three months," it said.
Uganda exported a record 1.45 million 60-kg bags of coffee in 1995/96.

"While it is not expected that it will be possible to achieve the same figure this season, it is encouraging to have seen such a strong response to the liberalisation of the industry," Schluter said. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
